title: The Television Sixties
tagline: Suburbs, tail fins and a television in most living rooms.

morningRoutine.detail: Breakfast-time television in black and white: morning shows had been on the air since 1952, and about 46 million households owned a set.

source.label: Wikipedia: Today (American TV program)

morningRoutine.detail: Gasoline averaged about 31 cents a gallon and 74 million motor vehicles were on the road, so suburban families drove to work.

source.label: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Annual Energy Review, Table 5.24: Retail Motor Gasoline and On-Highway Diesel Fuel Prices, 1949–2011

places.title: The front page
places.description: The Cold War, civil rights and the Kennedy–Nixon election, with the first televised presidential debates, dominated the news.
places.imageAlt: A mid-century newspaper front page with a large photo and bold sans-serif headlines
highlights: Kennedy and Nixon meet in televised debates
U-2 spy plane shot down over the Soviet Union

source.label: Wikipedia: 1960 in the United States

technology.name: Rotary-dial telephone
technology.description: A heavy desk phone in about 78% of homes. Long distance was expensive: three daytime minutes from New York to San Francisco cost $2.25.

source.label: U.S. Census Bureau, Historical Statistics of the United States, Colonial Times to 1970, series R 13–16: telephone toll rates from New York City

technology.name: The family car
technology.description: Big and heavy, with bench seats; 74 million motor vehicles were registered and gasoline cost about 31 cents a gallon.

source.label: FHWA Highway Statistics Summary to 1995, Table MV-200: State Motor Vehicle Registrations, 1900–1995

technology.name: Mainframe computer
technology.description: Room-sized machines fed with punched cards; new business models announced in late 1959 brought them to banks, insurers and government offices.

source.label: Wikipedia: IBM 1401

futureVisions.prediction: People and computers will soon work together in real time, the computer handling routine work while the person sets goals and judges results.
futureVisions.whoSaidIt: J. C. R. Licklider, "Man-Computer Symbiosis", IRE Transactions on Human Factors in Electronics, March 1960
futureVisions.note: Interactive computing, from time-sharing to personal computers, grew out of research he later funded.

source.label: Wikipedia: J. C. R. Licklider

futureVisions.prediction: If human population keeps growing as it has for two thousand years, it will approach infinity on Friday, 13 November 2026.
futureVisions.whoSaidIt: Heinz von Foerster and colleagues, "Doomsday: Friday, 13 November, A.D. 2026", Science, November 1960
futureVisions.note: Growth slowed instead: the world passed 8 billion people in November 2022, and the date is only weeks away.

source.label: Wikipedia: Heinz von Foerster

futureVisions.prediction: A new three-person spacecraft, Apollo, will carry astronauts on flights such as a trip around the Moon.
futureVisions.whoSaidIt: NASA, announcing the Apollo program to industry, July 1960
futureVisions.note: Apollo 8 circled the Moon in December 1968 and Apollo 11 landed in July 1969.

source.label: Wikipedia: Apollo program
